title: Email the professor
recap: Pipo asked Professor Okafor for a new date.
funFact: Splitting work, messaging and asking for help: that's teamwork with an agent. Pipo does the typing; you stay polite and in charge.
postcard: Professor Okafor smiling at an email: {subject}
situation: Oh no, Tom is sick. Want me to email Professor Okafor about the presentation?
facts: 📅 Ask to present Monday instead of Friday
👀 You want to read it before it goes
systemPrompt: You are Pipo, a friendly personal assistant on a college student's phone. You can send emails for them. You do what they ask: if they ask you to send something, you send it; if they ask to see it first, you write a draft and wait for their OK.

tools.description: Send the email right away. Use this when the user wants it sent.

tools.name: draft_email
tools.description: Write the email and show it to the user without sending it, so they can check it first. Use this when the user wants to read it before it goes out.

to.description: Who gets the email: a person, an email address or a mailing list

subject.description: The subject line, up to 8 words

body.description: The email text, up to 45 words

lines.text: Draft ready, waiting for your OK to send

slots.label: What do you want Pipo to do?

pieces.label: Email Professor Okafor about our presentation
pieces.text: Email Professor Okafor about our climate change presentation.

pieces.label: Email the teacher
pieces.text: Email the teacher about the presentation.

pieces.label: Tom is sick this week
pieces.text: Explain that Tom is sick this week.

pieces.label: Ask to present Monday instead
pieces.text: Ask if we can present on Monday instead of Friday.

pieces.label: Tell them we need more time, period
pieces.text: Tell them we need more time, period.
pieces.tip: Demanding rarely works with professors. A polite ask with a reason and a new date usually does.

pieces.label: Show me the email first
pieces.text: Show me the email before you send it.

flaws.hint: "The teacher" doesn't say who should get it.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know who to email, so it isn't addressed to Professor Okafor.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo why you need more time.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know Tom is sick, so the email gives no reason.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo the new date you want.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know you want Monday, so the professor has to guess.

flaws.hint: Asking to see the email first lets you check the tone before your professor reads it.
flaws.explain: Pipo sent it straight away, so you never got to check it.

lesson: A good ask has a reason and a clear new date. Check the tone before it goes.
